description: Initial third-contract generalization set for the official MeitY Master Service Agreement procurement template. This is a template, not an executed transaction-specific contract.

source_documents.provenance: Official MeitY/eGov Standards source: https://egovstandards.gov.in/sites/default/files/2026-03/Guidelines%20for%20Master%20Service%20Agreement.pdf; CONTRACT_TEMPLATE / MASTER_SERVICE_AGREEMENT_TEMPLATE, not an executed contract.

cases.question: What parties does this MSA define for the agreement?
cases.expected_answer: The MSA defines the parties as the Purchaser and the Managed Service Provider.

expected_evidence.anchor: Parties means Purchaser and Managed Service Provider

cases.question: How does the document define the services covered by the MSA?
cases.expected_answer: Services are delivered to the Purchaser's stakeholders and nominated agencies using tangible and intangible assets managed and operated by the Managed Service Provider.

expected_evidence.anchor: Services means the services delivered to the Stakeholders

cases.question: What does the document mean by a Service Level?
cases.expected_answer: A Service Level means the level of service and other performance criteria applying to the Services delivered by the Managed Service Provider.

expected_evidence.anchor: Service Level means the level of service and other performance criteria

cases.question: Which components are included in the defined SLA?
cases.expected_answer: The defined SLA includes Availability, Performance, Security, Support, Helpdesk, Disaster Recovery, Audit, Monitoring, and other SLAs executed as part of the MSA.

expected_evidence.anchor: SLA means the Availability, Performance, Security, Support, Helpdesk

cases.question: When does the agreement begin and what event ends its ordinary term?
cases.expected_answer: It begins on the stated Effective Date and continues until the operation and maintenance completion date unless terminated earlier.

expected_evidence.anchor: shall continue till operation and maintenance completion date

cases.question: What must the Purchaser provide to help test the system or application?
cases.expected_answer: The Purchaser or its nominated agencies must provide personnel support to test the system, application, or solution during the term.

expected_evidence.anchor: provide any support through personnel to test the system

cases.question: What must the Managed Service Provider provide to the Purchaser?
cases.expected_answer: The Managed Service Provider must provide the Deliverables specified by the Purchaser.

expected_evidence.anchor: It shall provide to the Purchaser or its nominated agencies, the Deliverables

cases.question: What standard must the provider meet when performing the Services?
cases.expected_answer: The provider must perform in a good and workmanlike manner consistent with applicable industry and technical standards, comply with Service Levels, and follow the Purchaser's Project Timelines.

expected_evidence.anchor: perform the Services in a good and workmanlike manner commensurate
comply with the applicable Service Levels

targets.anchor: perform the Services in a good and workmanlike manner commensurate
comply with the applicable Service Levels

cases.question: How is the amount payable for Cloud Services determined?
cases.expected_answer: The Purchaser pays for actual consumption of Cloud Services, using the applicable pricing model and discovered unit prices.

expected_evidence.anchor: shall pay to the Managed Service Provider for the actual consumption

cases.question: Can the provider increase the Cloud Services fee during the project?
cases.expected_answer: The provider may not increase the fee during the project unless the Cloud Contract contains an agreed provision allowing it.

expected_evidence.anchor: shall not increase the fee of the Cloud Services

cases.question: What is the normal payment period after receipt of an invoice and supporting documents?
cases.expected_answer: Payment is to be made within 30 working days of receipt of the invoice and supporting documents, subject to applicable deductions.

expected_evidence.anchor: Payment shall be made within <30 working days> of the receipt of invoice

cases.question: What financial consequences can affect payments under the agreement?
cases.expected_answer: Payments may be subject to liquidated damages or SLA penalties and related adjustments or corrections provided for in the MSA or SLA.

expected_evidence.anchor: Payments shall be subject to the application of liquidated damages or SLA penalties

cases.question: What security and safety requirements apply to the provider?
cases.expected_answer: The provider must comply with applicable security and safety requirements under the IT Act or Telegraph Act, the Purchaser's IT Security Manual, and relevant industry standards.

expected_evidence.anchor: comply with the technical requirements of the relevant security, safety

cases.question: What must the parties report about unauthorized access attempts?
cases.expected_answer: The parties should report in writing identified attempts by unauthorized persons to access or interfere with data, facilities, or Confidential Information.

expected_evidence.anchor: report forthwith in writing to each other all identified attempts

cases.question: What audit right does the Purchaser have over the provider and its facilities?
cases.expected_answer: The Purchaser or its nominated agency may audit and inspect the provider, agents, third-party facilities, data centres, documents, records, procedures, and systems to the extent reasonably necessary to verify service provision.

expected_evidence.anchor: shall have the right to audit and inspect Managed Service Provider

cases.question: What safeguards are required for sensitive or confidential data?
cases.expected_answer: Sensitive, confidential, or restricted data must be encrypted using an appropriate security process and approved key-management options suited to the Purchaser's requirements.

expected_evidence.anchor: data is encrypted as part of a standard security process

cases.question: What must the provider do after a security incident or intrusion?
cases.expected_answer: The provider must promptly notify the Purchaser of security incidents, intrusions, or requests by foreign governments or their agencies for access to data.

expected_evidence.anchor: shall notify the Purchaser promptly in the event of security incidents or intrusions

cases.question: What confidentiality duty applies to Purchaser data?
cases.expected_answer: The provider must maintain the confidentiality, integrity, availability, and privacy of Purchaser data and execute an NDA with the Purchaser.

expected_evidence.anchor: shall maintain confidentiality, integrity, availability and privacy of the Purchaser data

cases.question: Where must the provider store data under the MSA?
cases.expected_answer: The provider must store all types of data within Indian Territory and may not take data outside India unless explicitly approved by the Purchaser.

expected_evidence.anchor: shall store all types of data
within the Indian Territory

targets.anchor: shall store all types of data

cases.question: Who owns data created as part of the project?
cases.expected_answer: The Purchaser owns all data created as part of the project without exceptions.

expected_evidence.anchor: All the data created as the part of the project shall be owned by Purchaser

cases.question: What backup duties does the Managed Service Provider have?
cases.expected_answer: The provider must configure, schedule, and manage backups of the listed data and systems according to the Purchaser's or MeitY's policy.

expected_evidence.anchor: shall configure, schedule and manage backups of all the data

cases.question: What happens to newly created intellectual property developed solely during performance?
cases.expected_answer: The Purchaser owns and may use in perpetuity newly created IPR arising solely during execution, and the provider must disclose and transfer it as required.

expected_evidence.anchor: shall own and have a right in perpetuity to use all newly created Intellectual Property Rights

cases.question: Who retains pre-existing intellectual property rights?
cases.expected_answer: Pre-existing intellectual property remains with the party that owned it before the Effective Date, subject to the Purchaser's stated license rights for project documents and materials.

expected_evidence.anchor: All intellectual property rights existing prior to the Effective Date

cases.question: What is the general liability cap for claims related to the agreement?
cases.expected_answer: Liability is limited to direct damages and, generally, may not exceed one time the total contract value, subject to the stated indemnification and security-breach exceptions.

expected_evidence.anchor: shall be the payment of direct damages only which shall in no event exceed one time the total contract value

cases.provenance: Indemnification and Limitation of Liability, page 29

cases.question: Which obligations are outside the general liability cap?
cases.expected_answer: The general cap does not apply to indemnification obligations or breach of Clause 1.11.4.

expected_evidence.anchor: shall not be applicable to the indemnification obligations

cases.provenance: Indemnification and Limitation of Liability, page 29

cases.question: What cure notice applies to a material breach?
cases.expected_answer: The aggrieved party may give one month's notice to cure the material breach; if it continues after the notice period, the relevant party may terminate.

expected_evidence.anchor: terminate this Agreement upon giving a one month�s notice for curing the Material Breach

cases.question: What notice is specified when SLA failure constitutes material breach?
cases.expected_answer: For an SLA failure that constitutes material breach, the Purchaser may give a 30-day written notice to cure it, followed by a termination option if it continues.

expected_evidence.anchor: serve a 30 days written notice for curing this Material Breach

cases.question: Can the Purchaser terminate the contract for convenience?
cases.expected_answer: Yes. The Purchaser may terminate the Contract at any time for any reason by giving the provider a notice of termination referring to the convenience clause.

expected_evidence.anchor: may at any time terminate the Contract for any reason

cases.question: What transition obligations apply when the agreement ends?
cases.expected_answer: The provider must support transition and migration, prepare or follow an Exit Management Plan, migrate VMs and data to the new environment, and keep required documentation current and hand it over.

expected_evidence.anchor: responsible for both transition of the services as well as migration of the VMs, Data, Content
all the documentation required by the Purchaser for smooth transition

targets.anchor: responsible for both transition of the services as well as migration of the VMs, Data, Content
all the documentation required by the Purchaser for smooth transition

cases.question: What document supplies the applicable service levels?
cases.expected_answer: The Model Service Level Agreements referenced on the MeghRaj webpage apply to the provider and form part of the MSA.

expected_evidence.anchor: shall be applicable to Managed Service Provider and is part of this Agreement

cases.question: What law and court jurisdiction apply to the agreement?
cases.expected_answer: The agreement is construed under applicable Indian law, and legal disputes are subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of courts where the Purchaser is located.

expected_evidence.anchor: construed in accordance with IT Act and Regulations, Privacy laws and other applicable laws of India

cases.provenance: Applicable Law and Dispute Resolution, page 42

cases.question: What is the escalation path if a dispute is not resolved initially?
cases.expected_answer: The process moves from escalation to mediation, then potentially to a panel of three experts, and finally to arbitration if unresolved.

expected_evidence.anchor: both the parties should agree on a mediator
a neutral panel of 3 experts
then the matter should be referred to Arbitration

targets.anchor: both the parties should agree on a mediator
then the matter should be referred to Arbitration

cases.provenance: Applicable Law and Dispute Resolution, page 42

cases.question: Which provisions could expose the provider to financial risk?
cases.expected_answer: Potential financial exposure includes liquidated damages or SLA penalties deducted from payments, direct-damage liability subject to the stated cap and exceptions, and excess replacement-service costs after material breach.

expected_evidence.anchor: liquidated damages or SLA penalties
direct damages only
liable to the Purchaser for any excess costs

targets.anchor: liable to the Purchaser for any excess costs

cases.question: What could create operational or compliance exposure for the provider?
cases.expected_answer: Potential exposure includes security and privacy failures, audit findings, unauthorized data access or disclosure, and non-compliance with Indian data-location and reporting requirements.

expected_evidence.anchor: secure the Purchaser�s data and content
within the Indian Territory
right to audit and inspect

targets.anchor: secure the Purchaser�s data and content

cases.provenance: Security, data location, and audit provisions

cases.question: What exact Cloud Services price was awarded to the provider?
cases.expected_answer: The exact awarded price cannot be determined from this template because commercial proposal values are placeholders or project-specific inputs.
cases.provenance: Template document; no executed commercial award

cases.question: Which named company was selected as the Managed Service Provider?
cases.expected_answer: The selected company cannot be determined because this is a reusable procurement template rather than an executed transaction-specific agreement.
cases.provenance: Template document; provider identity is not filled in

cases.question: What exact project commencement date applies to this MSA?
cases.expected_answer: No exact project commencement date can be determined because the Effective Date is a template placeholder to be completed for a project.
cases.provenance: Term and Duration contains an Effective Date placeholder

cases.question: What uptime percentage does the provider owe under the SLA?
cases.expected_answer: The exact uptime percentage cannot be determined from this MSA alone because it refers to model SLAs and project-specific service-level terms.
cases.provenance: The MSA references Model Service Level Agreements without specifying an uptime value
